Daily setup

What to record (every day)
- Bulk cues: puffy/smoother/looser feel, gentle bubbles under the surface, stretches easily during folds vs dense/tight (under) or slack/watery and won’t hold shape (over).
- Proof cues: lighter and gently wobbly; poke springs back slowly vs firm/fast spring (under) or a dent that doesn’t recover and fragile look (over).

Day 1 — Baseline
- Both A and B: your normal process and flour. Just practice reading the bulk and proof cues above and writing them down.

Day 2 — Temperature effect
- A: warmer spot; B: cooler spot.
- Compare how fast each reaches the same cues. Warmer moves faster; cooler slows things down and gives flavor more time to develop.

Day 3 — Hydration effect
- A: your usual feel; B: wetter dough.
- Expect the wetter dough to look wobblier and “done” earlier. Judge by airy softness (good) vs merely wet. When truly over, it turns soupy and hard to handle.

Day 4 — Flour choice (white vs whole‑grain/rye)
- A: mostly white flour; B: add whole‑grain/rye.
- The whole‑grain/rye dough ferments faster, feels stickier/pasty even when it’s fine, and shows fewer big bubbles. Look for a gentle puff, slight dome, and a more velvety/settled feel. Over goes gummy; under stays dense and clay‑like.

Day 5 — Bulk endpoints (under vs over on purpose)
- A: stop bulk early; B: push bulk longer.
- Feel the contrast: A should be dense/tight and resistant; B gets slack/watery at the edges and won’t hold shape during a fold. Note how that sets up the proof stage.

Day 6 — Acidity balance
- A: a shorter, more moderate bulk; B: a longer bulk to build more acidity.
- Acidity helps flavor and can strengthen feel up to a point; too much makes dough sluggish and weak. Compare elasticity/bounce vs sluggishness, then carry both into proof and use the poke test.

Day 7 — Synthesis run
- Choose the combo you liked best from the week (temp, hydration, flour). Run one focused batch and aim to hit ideal bulk and proof cues without checking the clock. Write a short summary of the exact signs you used.

Optional notes to add to your log
- For high‑hydration doughs: note when “airy” crosses into “soupy.”
- For whole‑grain/rye: note the shift from tacky to velvety/settled; watch for gummy (over) vs clay‑like (under).
- For proof: record jiggle/wobble and the poke‑test recovery each time.
